target_customer: Small and mid-size manufacturers and workshops that want a low-cost programmable robot arm
problem: Industrial robot arms are expensive and hard to program; the founders first saw painting and sanding furniture as slow and costly manual work.
business_model: Robots as a service arms (a directory cites from 1500 dollars per month, unverified) plus hardware sales and the RoboGPT programming layer
product_category: Low-cost collaborative robot arms with AI programming

founders.name: Abhinav Das
founders.background_notes: YC page profile title reads builder of robots, trucks and other machines. YourStory (Dec 2025) per search summary names him CEO.

founders.name: Akash Bansal
founders.background_notes: Named by the YC page and TechCrunch (Aug 2023).

founders.name: Aditya Bhatia
founders.background_notes: Named by the YC page and TechCrunch (Aug 2023).

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing a safe, accurate and cheap robot arm needs mechanical, control and software work; a small team using automotive parts to cut cost is hard in 2018.

defensibility.rationale: Cheap arms and programming software were being built by several players, and no proprietary data or contracts are documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rethink Robotics closed in October 2018 per MIT Technology Review via search summary; no incumbent acquired or copied Orangewood in sources found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch says the founders in late 2017 found furniture painting and sanding incredibly time-consuming and costly, which led to a remotely operated painting arm.

branding.domain_note: Uses orangewood.co; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mass-market and bold: Democratizing Robots and ROBOTS ARE HERE

branding.community_and_virality: Site advertises a developer community signup; no independent evidence of fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself beyond a 2023 TechCrunch story and trade coverage.

pivots.from: Remotely operated robot arm for painting furniture
pivots.to: General low-cost robot arm with RoboGPT natural language programming for inspection, powder coating and picking
pivots.why: TechCrunch describes an expansion to more use cases enabled by RoboGPT; it does not call it a pivot.

outcome_analysis: Orangewood started in late 2017 with a remotely operated furniture painting arm and joined YC in Winter 2018. Public funding is thin: a 4.5 million dollar tranche led by YC was reported in August 2023, with a larger equity raise said to be pending. It is still operating with a small team and no clear verdict on success yet.
notes: Competitor list left empty: no source dated at or before the Winter 2018 batch naming Orangewood competitors was found; Ally, named by TechCrunch in 2023, is too late. Aggregators (CB Insights, Seedtable) label the 2023 round Series A or seed and give totals of 4.1 to 4.7 million dollars; TechCrunch gives no label so stage is other. No earlier rounds found. YourStory claim of a CNC machine origin and a 1 million dollar revenue claim are from search summaries and unverified.
